Why the best websites leave a little room to breathe.

Space isn’t what’s left over. It’s one of the most useful tools a designer has.

In this article
Space helps people chooseFind a rhythmEdit before you decorate

Written byThe Relay teamIdeas and observations from our independent digital studio.

Space helps people choose

A crowded page asks everything to compete at once. Generous spacing creates a hierarchy: what to notice first, what to read next and where to go from there.

The aim is not minimalism for its own sake. It is to give every important piece of information the attention it deserves.

Find a rhythm

A website needs changes of pace. A large photograph can follow a dense explanation. A short statement can give someone a moment to absorb what they have just read.

Consistent spacing makes that rhythm feel intentional. It also helps the experience hold together as the layout changes from a large screen to a phone.

Edit before you decorate

When a section feels weak, the answer is not always another border, icon or effect. Sometimes it needs a clearer sentence and fewer things around it.

Good design often comes from knowing what to leave out, then giving what remains enough room to work.
